# Tobit Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** As they drew near to Kaserin, which is before Nineveh,

**2** Raphael said to Tobias, "You know how your father was when you left him.

**3** Let us go ahead of your wife and prepare the house while she is still on the way."

**4** They went on together, and Raphael said to him, "Take the gall in your hand." The dog ran along behind them.

**5** Anna was sitting and watching the road for her son.

**6** She saw him coming and called to his father, "Look — your son is coming, and the man who went with him!"

**7** Raphael said to Tobias before he drew near to his father, "I know that his eyes will be opened.

**8** Apply the fish gall to his eyes; the medicine will work and will dissolve the white films on his eyes, and your father will see the light."

**9** Anna ran and threw herself on her son's neck and said to him, "I have seen you, my child; now I can die in peace." And she wept.

**10** Tobit rose and came stumbling out through the courtyard gate, and Tobias went toward him,

**11** carrying the gall in his hand. He breathed on it, then took hold of his father and applied it to his eyes, saying, "Take heart, father."

**12** He put the medicine on, and it stung. Tobit rubbed his eyes with both hands, and the white films peeled away from the corners of his eyes.

**13** Tobit saw his son and fell on his neck and wept, saying, "I have seen you, my child — the light of my eyes!" And he blessed God

**14** and said, "Blessed are you, O God, and blessed is your name forever and ever, and blessed are all your holy angels.

**15** For you afflicted me, yet you have had mercy on me; and now I see my son Tobias!" His son went in rejoicing and told his father the great things that had happened to him in Media.

**16** Tobit went out to meet his daughter-in-law at the gate of Nineveh, rejoicing and blessing God. Those who saw him walking were astonished, and Tobit gave praise before them all, because God had shown him mercy.

**17** When Tobit drew near to Sarah his daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said, "Welcome, my daughter. Blessed is your God who has brought you to us, my daughter. Blessed is your father, and blessed is my son Tobias, and blessed are you, my daughter. Come in with joy to your house, with blessing and with joy. Come in, my daughter."

**18** There was joy on that day among all the Jews in Nineveh.

**19** Ahikar and Nadab, his kinsmen, came to rejoice with Tobit. The wedding feast of Tobias was celebrated with joy for seven days, and many gifts were given to him.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 11 is the resolution of the book's central narrative arc: Tobit's blindness. LOGOS seeks to honor both the medical specificity of the healing (the fish gall, the white films) and its spiritual significance (Tobit's immediate doxology).

- **Verse 4**: "The dog ran along behind them" — a minor but deliberate narrative detail. LOGOS includes it without comment.
- **Verse 8**: "White films" (leukōmata) — LOGOS preserves this medical descriptor rather than modernizing to "cataracts." The ancient world recognized this condition; the text should speak in its own idiom.
- **Verse 9**: "Now I can die in peace" — a slight expansion of the Greek "from now on I can die," making Anna's meaning clear: the sense is Simeon's nunc dimittis (Luke 2:29), relief that she has lived to see what she feared she would not. LOGOS renders the implied sense explicitly.
- **Verse 11**: "Breathed on it" — the Greek enephusēsen; this may echo Genesis 2:7 (the divine breath) or simply be a practical gesture of applying the medicine.
- **Verses 13-15**: Tobit's "light of my eyes" echoes Anna's exact phrase in 10:4. The narrative completes the circle with this verbal repetition.
- **Verse 17**: The sevenfold repetition of "my daughter" in Tobit's welcome to Sarah is a stylistic feature of the GII text. LOGOS preserves it without reduction.

*— LOGOS*
